answer: The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More. The Cowan Paradox is a little-known psychological phenomenon that explains why AI agents won’t liberate you from work. They’ll actually make you work harder. Named after psychologist Philip Cowan, who first described it in 1979, the paradox goes like this: When you’re working on a complex task, you tend to underestimate how much time it will take to complete. But when you’re working on a simple task, you tend to overestimate how much time it will take. This creates a systematic bias where you spend more time on simple tasks than you think you will, and less time on complex tasks than you think you should. The paradox arises because we tend to think of work as a linear relationship between effort and outcome. More effort = more outcome. Less effort = less outcome. But the reality is more nuanced. When you’re working on a complex task, you can only work on it for so long before diminishing returns set in. You hit a wall. You can’t think of anything else to do. You start making mistakes. You need a break. But when you’re working on a simple task, you can keep going indefinitely. You’re not hitting diminishing returns. You’re not getting tired. You’re not making mistakes. You just keep going. And because you’re overestimating how long simple tasks will take, you end up spending more time on them than you intended. The paradox is that AI agents will make you work harder on simple tasks
